Case 1: a small circle at A and a larger circle at B touching on AB.
Case 2: the same two circles with a clear gap between them on AB.
Case 3: the same two circles overlapping in a lens.
Case 1 again, with the touching point on AB labelled X (sum of the two radii = AB).
Case 2 again, with a small clear gap on AB (sum of the two radii < AB).
Case 3 again, overlapping, with the arrows 'radius 1' and 'radius 2' on AB.
Printed answer of Figure it Out 7.2 Q1: a circle with its centre and two points on its lower part joined to the centre and to each other (an isosceles triangle with apex at the centre).
Printed answer of Figure it Out 7.2 Q2, first figure: two equal circles with crossing points C and D, AB, AC, BC, AD, BD drawn, and extra points C1 to C3 and D1 to D3 on the circles.

Printed answer of Figure it Out 7.2 Q2, second figure: three equal circles with only A, B (centres), C (top crossing) and D (lower crossing, also the third centre) lettered, no segments. The LP solution keeps the question's lettering instead.
